questions.explanation: Athlete's foot is a fungal infection; keeping feet clean and dry helps prevent it.

questions.stem: Sickle cell disease is
questions.explanation: Sickle cell disease is inherited from both parents through their genes; it is not infectious.

questions.stem: A person whose genotype is AS is said to be a
options: sickle cell patient with frequent crises
carrier of the sickle cell trait
questions.explanation: AS people carry one sickle gene but usually have no symptoms; they can pass it on.

questions.stem: If both parents have the genotype AS, there is a chance that their child will have the genotype
questions.explanation: Each AS parent can pass on the S gene, so a child may inherit SS (about a 1 in 4 chance for each pregnancy).

questions.stem: Which of these helps a person with sickle cell disease to reduce crises?
options: Drinking plenty of water and avoiding extreme cold
questions.explanation: Good hydration, warmth, rest, malaria prevention and regular medical care help reduce crises.

questions.stem: Kwashiorkor in children is caused mainly by lack of
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor results from severe protein deficiency, causing swelling, a pot belly and pale, thin hair.

questions.stem: Asthma is a condition in which
options: the airways become narrow and inflamed, causing difficulty in breathing
questions.explanation: Asthma attacks are triggered by dust, smoke, allergens or exercise and are managed with inhalers.

questions.stem: Obesity is a condition of
options: excess body fat that is harmful to health
questions.explanation: Obesity is excessive fat accumulation that raises the risk of diabetes, heart disease and joint problems.

questions.stem: Which lifestyle change BEST helps to prevent obesity?
options: Eating a balanced diet and exercising regularly
Sitting for long hours watching television
Skipping breakfast and overeating at night
questions.explanation: Balanced eating and regular physical activity keep energy intake and use in balance.

questions.stem: Anaemia is a condition in which a person has
options: too little haemoglobin or too few red blood cells
questions.explanation: Anaemia reduces the oxygen-carrying capacity of blood, causing tiredness and pallor.

questions.stem: Elephantiasis (lymphatic filariasis) is transmitted by the
questions.explanation: Culex mosquitoes transmit the worms that cause lymphatic filariasis.

questions.stem: Yellow fever is transmitted by the
questions.explanation: Aedes mosquitoes transmit yellow fever and dengue; vaccination prevents yellow fever.

questions.stem: The housefly spreads diseases such as cholera and dysentery mainly by
options: carrying germs on its legs and body from filth to food
questions.explanation: Houseflies are mechanical vectors that carry germs from faeces and refuse to food.

questions.stem: Mosquito larvae live and develop in
questions.explanation: Mosquitoes lay eggs on still water, where larvae and pupae develop.

questions.stem: Spreading a thin layer of oil on stagnant water controls mosquitoes by
options: preventing larvae and pupae from breathing at the surface
making the water cleaner for drinking
questions.explanation: The oil film blocks the breathing tubes of larvae and pupae, killing them.

questions.stem: Anopheles mosquito larvae can be distinguished from Culex larvae because Anopheles larvae
options: hang at an angle from the surface
lie parallel to the water surface
questions.explanation: Anopheles larvae rest parallel to the surface, while Culex larvae hang at an angle by a breathing siphon.

questions.stem: Which of these is a vector control measure?
options: Clearing bushes and draining stagnant water around the house
Leaving old tyres full of water
questions.explanation: Removing breeding sites reduces mosquito and other vector populations.

questions.stem: Measles spreads from person to person mainly through
options: droplets in the air when an infected person coughs or sneezes
questions.explanation: Measles is highly contagious and spreads through airborne droplets; vaccination prevents it.

questions.stem: HIV CANNOT be transmitted through
options: from an infected mother to her baby
questions.explanation: HIV is not spread by casual contact like handshakes, hugging or sharing plates.

questions.stem: The medicines that keep HIV under control in an infected person are called
questions.explanation: Antiretroviral therapy suppresses HIV and allows people living with HIV to live long, healthy lives.

questions.stem: Frequent illness of a parent can affect the family by
options: reducing family income and increasing medical costs
questions.explanation: Illness reduces earning capacity and adds expenses, burdening the family.

questions.stem: Which choice BEST protects a young person from sexually transmitted infections?
questions.explanation: For young people, abstinence is the surest protection against STIs and HIV.

questions.stem: Disease transmission means
options: the passing of disease-causing germs from one person or animal to another
questions.explanation: Transmission is how pathogens spread, directly or through vectors, air, water or food.

questions.stem: The immediate help given to an injured or sick person before medical help arrives is called
questions.explanation: First aid is the initial care that preserves life and prevents the condition from getting worse.

questions.stem: For a nosebleed, the casualty should
options: sit up, lean forward and pinch the soft part of the nose
questions.explanation: Leaning forward prevents swallowing blood; pinching the soft part of the nose for about 10 minutes helps it stop.

questions.stem: Why should a first aider wear gloves when treating a bleeding wound?
options: To make the wound bleed more
To protect both the casualty and the first aider from infection
questions.explanation: Gloves form a barrier against blood-borne infections for both people.

questions.stem: A player suffering from a muscle cramp during a match should
options: gently stretch and massage the affected muscle
take a painkiller and keep playing
questions.explanation: Stretching and gentle massage relieve cramp; rest and fluids also help.

questions.stem: For a suspected broken leg, the first aider should
options: try to straighten the bone by pulling
support and keep the leg still with a splint and seek medical help
make the casualty walk on it
questions.explanation: Immobilising the limb prevents further injury; never try to reset a fracture.

questions.stem: Before helping a person who is receiving an electric shock, the rescuer must first
options: switch off the power or separate the person with a dry non-conducting object
pull the person away with bare hands
touch the person to check the pulse
questions.explanation: Touching someone still in contact with current can electrocute the rescuer.

questions.stem: Which of these should NOT be applied to a burn?
questions.explanation: Greasy substances trap heat and cause infection; cool the burn with running water instead.

questions.stem: At the scene of a road crash, the FIRST thing a helper should do is
options: make sure the scene is safe and call for help
give the victims water to drink
questions.explanation: Ensuring safety and calling emergency services comes first; injured people should not be moved unless in immediate danger.

questions.stem: The FRSC toll-free number that can be called to report a road crash is
questions.explanation: The FRSC emergency number is 122; 112 is the general national emergency number.

questions.stem: Which of these is a cause of domestic accidents?
options: Leaving sharp knives and medicines within children's reach
questions.explanation: Careless storage of sharp objects, medicines and chemicals causes injuries and poisoning at home.

questions.stem: A child has swallowed a household chemical. The first aider should
options: make the child vomit by putting fingers in the throat
give the child palm oil to drink
seek medical help at once and take the container along, without forcing the child to vomit
wait to see if symptoms appear
questions.explanation: Inducing vomiting can cause more damage with corrosive substances; get medical help quickly and show the product.

questions.stem: A person who feels faint should
options: lie down with the legs raised
questions.explanation: Lying down with legs raised helps blood flow back to the brain.

questions.stem: Chioma Ajunwa is remembered as the first Nigerian woman to
questions.explanation: She won long jump gold at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics, the first Olympic gold for a Nigerian woman.

questions.stem: Hogan "Kid" Bassey is remembered as
questions.explanation: Hogan Bassey won the world featherweight boxing title in 1957.

questions.stem: Dick Tiger was a Nigerian world champion in
questions.explanation: Dick Tiger held world middleweight and light heavyweight boxing titles in the 1960s.

questions.stem: Nigeria won its first-ever Olympic medal, a bronze in boxing, at the
questions.explanation: Nojeem Maiyegun won bronze in boxing at Tokyo 1964, Nigeria's first Olympic medal.

questions.stem: Nigeria's Golden Eaglets became the first African team to win a FIFA world tournament when they won the U-17 World Cup in
questions.explanation: The Golden Eaglets won the first FIFA U-16 (now U-17) World Championship in China in 1985.

questions.stem: The Super Falcons are Nigeria's
questions.explanation: The Super Falcons have won the African women's championship more times than any other team.

questions.stem: Rashidi Yekini is remembered for scoring
options: the winning goal in the 1996 Olympic final
the first goal at the 1980 Africa Cup final
Nigeria's first goal at a FIFA World Cup, in 1994
a world record in long jump
questions.explanation: Yekini scored Nigeria's first World Cup goal against Bulgaria at USA 1994.

questions.stem: A person who trains in physical education and teaches it in schools is a
questions.explanation: PE teachers are professionals who teach physical and health education.

questions.stem: Which of these is a career in physical education and sports?
questions.explanation: Careers in PE include coaching, teaching, sports administration, physiotherapy and sports journalism.

questions.stem:
(a) What is physical fitness? [2 marks]
(b) List two health-related and two performance-related components of physical fitness. [4 marks]
(c) State four safety precautions to observe while exercising. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) The ability of the body to carry out daily tasks efficiently without undue fatigue and still have energy for emergencies
1 mark: (b) Health-related: cardiovascular endurance / muscular strength
1 mark: (b) Health-related: flexibility / muscular endurance / body composition
1 mark: (b) Performance-related: speed / agility
1 mark: (b) Performance-related: balance / power / coordination / reaction time
1 mark: (c) Warm up before and cool down after exercise
1 mark: (c) Wear suitable clothing and shoes
1 mark: (c) Do not exercise when ill or injured / immediately after a heavy meal
1 mark: (c) Increase workload gradually / drink water / exercise under supervision
questions.explanation: Accept any two correct components in each group and any four sensible precautions.

questions.stem:
(a) Differentiate among leisure, recreation and dance. [3 marks]
(b) Give two examples each of indoor and outdoor recreational activities. [4 marks]
(c) Name three Nigerian traditional dances and the people associated with each. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Leisure: free time when one is not working or studying
1 mark: (a) Recreation: enjoyable activities freely chosen in leisure time for refreshment
1 mark: (a) Dance: rhythmic movement of the body, usually to music
1 mark: (b) Indoor: table tennis
1 mark: (b) Indoor: ludo / draughts / scrabble / chess
1 mark: (b) Outdoor: hiking / picnicking
1 mark: (b) Outdoor: swimming / camping / fishing
1 mark: (c) Atilogwu: Igbo
1 mark: (c) Bata or Agidigbo: Yoruba
1 mark: (c) Sharo: Fulani / Langa: Hausa / Swange: Tiv
questions.explanation: Accept other correct traditional dances matched with the right people.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the terms "posture" and "postural defect". [4 marks]
(b) Name four postural defects. [4 marks]
(c) State two causes of postural defects. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Posture: the position in which the body is held when standing, sitting, walking or lying
2 marks: (a) Postural defect: an abnormal body position or curvature resulting from poor habits, poor nutrition or disease
1 mark: (b) Kyphosis
1 mark: (b) Lordosis
1 mark: (b) Scoliosis
1 mark: (b) Flat feet / bow legs / knock knees
1 mark: (c) Poor nutrition
1 mark: (c) Lack of exercise / poor sitting, walking or sleeping habits
questions.explanation: Causes listed in the syllabus are poor nutrition, lack of exercise and poor sitting, walking and sleeping habits.

questions.topic: Athletics (Track and Field): Group and Combined Events
questions.stem:
(a) What are combined events? [2 marks]
(b) List the ten events of the men's decathlon. [5 marks]
(c) How is the winner of a combined event decided? [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Competitions in which each athlete takes part in several track and field events and the scores are added
1 mark: (b) 100 m and long jump

1 mark: (b) Discus and pole vault

1 mark: (c) Each performance is converted to points using scoring tables
1 mark: (c) The points from all events are added together
1 mark: (c) The athlete with the highest total points wins
questions.explanation: Award 1 mark for each correct pair of decathlon events.

questions.stem:

(b) Name four officials in a soccer match. [4 marks]
(c) State two values of playing soccer. [2 marks]

1 mark: (c) Promotes teamwork, discipline and friendship / can be a career

questions.stem:

(b) Name three items of equipment used in hockey. [3 marks]

questions.stem:
(a) State three basic techniques in boxing. [3 marks]

(c) Give four importance of taekwondo. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:

questions.stem:
(a) Name four swimming strokes. [4 marks]
(b) List three items of swimming equipment. [3 marks]
(c) State three safety rules for swimming. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Front crawl (freestyle)
1 mark: (a) Breaststroke

questions.topic: Striking Games (Table Tennis, Tennis and Badminton)
questions.stem:
(a) Name the equipment needed to play (i) table tennis (ii) badminton. [4 marks]
(b) State three basic skills common to striking games. [3 marks]
(c) Name three officials in striking games. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a)(i) Table tennis bat (paddle)

questions.stem:
(a) Differentiate between sewage and refuse. [2 marks]
(b) Describe three methods of refuse disposal. [6 marks]
(c) Name two components of the school health programme. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Sewage: liquid waste from toilets, bathrooms and kitchens
1 mark: (a) Refuse: solid waste such as paper, cans, plastics and food remains
2 marks: (b) Incineration: burning refuse at high temperature in a furnace
2 marks: (b) Sanitary landfill: burying refuse in layers covered with soil
2 marks: (b) Composting: allowing organic waste to decay into manure / recycling: reprocessing waste into new products
1 mark: (c) Skill-based health education / school health services
1 mark: (c) Healthful school environment / school feeding / school-home-community relationship
questions.explanation: Award 1 mark for naming each method and 1 for describing it.

questions.stem:
(a) What is food? [2 marks]
(b) List the six classes of food nutrients and give one source of each. [6 marks]
(c) State two importance of food. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Any substance which, when eaten and digested, provides the body with energy and nutrients for growth and health
1 mark: (b) Carbohydrates, e.g. yam, rice, garri
1 mark: (b) Proteins, e.g. beans, fish, meat, eggs
1 mark: (b) Fats and oils, e.g. palm oil, groundnut oil
1 mark: (b) Vitamins, e.g. fruits and vegetables
1 mark: (b) Minerals and salts, e.g. milk, salt, green vegetables
1 mark: (b) Water
1 mark: (c) Provides energy for physical activities
1 mark: (c) Eliminates hunger / promotes growth and healthy living
questions.explanation: Award 1 mark for each nutrient class with a correct source.

questions.stem:
(a) What is a disease vector? [2 marks]
(b) Name three disease vectors and one disease each transmits. [3 marks]
(c) Describe the life cycle of the mosquito. [3 marks]
(d) State two ways of controlling mosquitoes. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) An organism, such as an insect, that carries and transmits pathogens from one host to another
1 mark: (b) Anopheles mosquito: malaria
1 mark: (b) Housefly: cholera / typhoid / dysentery
1 mark: (b) Tsetse fly: sleeping sickness / Aedes mosquito: yellow fever / blackfly: river blindness
1 mark: (c) Eggs are laid on stagnant water and hatch into larvae
1 mark: (c) Larvae develop into pupae in the water
1 mark: (c) Adults emerge from the pupae (egg, larva, pupa, adult)
1 mark: (d) Draining stagnant water / clearing bushes
1 mark: (d) Spraying insecticide / spreading oil on stagnant water / using treated nets
questions.explanation: Accept other correct vector-disease pairs and control measures.

questions.stem:
(a) Define (i) accident (ii) first aid. [4 marks]
(b) State three items found in a first aid box. [3 marks]
(c) Describe the first aid for a sprained ankle. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) An unexpected, unplanned event that may cause injury, damage or loss
2 marks: (a)(ii) The immediate help given to an injured or sick person before medical help arrives
1 mark: (b) Bandages / crepe bandage
1 mark: (b) Antiseptic solution / cotton wool / sterile dressings
1 mark: (b) Scissors / plaster / gloves / triangular bandage
1 mark: (c) Rest the ankle and stop activity
1 mark: (c) Apply ice wrapped in cloth and a compression bandage
1 mark: (c) Elevate the leg and seek medical help (RICE)
questions.explanation: The RICE method (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation) is the standard first aid for sprains.
